Smoky Stargazer Chili

Served at: Polaris Meteor Watch & UFO Evening

Serves 8-10Prep 25 minCook 1 hour 30 min

This hearty and warming Smoky Stargazer Chili is the perfect companion for a cool evening spent under the vast, star-studded sky, whether you're tracking meteors or scanning for unidentified aerial phenomena. Its deep, smoky flavors and comforting warmth make it an ideal dish to share with fellow sky-watchers, keeping everyone toasty and satisfied as you gaze into the cosmos.

Ingredients

  • 6 slices (170 g) thick-cut bacon, diced
  • 2 pounds (900 g) ground beef (80/20 lean)
  • 1 large (about 250 g) yellow onion, chopped
  • 1 medium (about 150 g) green bell pepper, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2-3 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, minced, plus 1 tablespoon (15 ml) adobo sauce
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) tomato paste
  • 3 tablespoons (45 ml) chili powder
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) smoked paprika
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) ground cumin
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) dried oregano
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) cayenne pepper (optional, for extra heat)
  • 1 (28 ounce / 794 g) can diced tomatoes, undrained
  • 1 (15 ounce / 425 g) can crushed tomatoes, undrained
  • 2 (15 ounce / 425 g) cans kidney beans, rinsed and drained
  • 2 cups (470 ml) beef broth
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Optional toppings: shredded cheddar cheese, sour cream, chopped fresh cilantro, sliced green onions, cornbread

Method

  1. In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
  2. Add the ground beef to the pot and cook over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain off any excess fat.
  3. Add the chopped onion and bell pepper to the pot and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
  4. Stir in the minced garlic, minced chipotle peppers, and adobo sauce. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
  5. Add the tomato paste, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, cocoa powder, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes to toast the spices.
  6. Stir in the diced tomatoes (with their liquid), crushed tomatoes, rinsed and drained kidney beans, and beef broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
  7. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let the chili simmer for at least 1 hour, stirring occasionally, to allow the flavors to meld. For a richer flavor, simmer for up to 2 hours.
  8. Stir in the reserved crispy bacon during the last 15 minutes of cooking, or use it as a topping.
  9. Taste and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper as needed.
  10. Serve hot with your favorite toppings.

Tips

  • Make Ahead: Chili often tastes even better the next day! Prepare it a day in advance and reheat gently before serving for deeper flavors.
  • Topping Bar: Set out a variety of toppings like shredded cheese, sour cream, fresh cilantro, and green onions so guests can customize their bowls.
  • Slow Cooker Option: After browning the meat and sautéing the aromatics and spices, transfer everything to a slow cooker. Cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours.
